resident.chief_complaint: Numbness and tingling in both hands that had severely aggravated in the few days before presentation.
resident.history: A 50-year-old male presented with numbness and tingling in both hands that had severely aggravated over a few days. For the preceding 6 months he reported an uncomfortable gait and inability to run due to clumsiness of the feet and weakened ankle strength. For 3 months before presentation, both hands began to feel numb and tingling, and the foot symptoms gradually worsened.
resident.physical_exam: General physical examination showed no abnormalities. Neurological examination identified grade IV power in flexion of both ankles and big toes, and hyperreflexia in all four limbs. Spurling's sign, Lhermitte's sign, and Hoffman's sign were absent. Sensory examination revealed slight diminution of pain and temperature sensitivity below the C5 dermatome, with posterior column sensation preserved.
key_positive_signs: Numbness and tingling in both hands
Grade IV power in flexion of both ankles and big toes
Diminished pain and temperature sensation below the C5 dermatome
Uncomfortable gait and inability to run due to foot clumsiness and ankle weakness
resident.past_history: No relevant medical or trauma history was reported.
resident.public_message: This is a 50-year-old male with a 6-month history of gait clumsiness, inability to run, and ankle weakness, and a 3-month history of numbness and tingling in both hands, which aggravated in the days before presentation. Examination showed grade IV power in ankle and big toe flexion, hyperreflexia in all four limbs, and diminished pain and temperature sensation below C5, with posterior column sensation preserved. Imaging showed loss of cervical lordosis, ossification of the nuchal ligament at C3-4, and a calcified left-sided ligamentum flavum at C5-6 causing nerve root and spinal cord compression, with hyperintense T2 cord signals at that level. No laboratory report is documented.

imaging.public_message: Reporting the case record's description only; the films were not available for review. CT and MRI described calcified/ossified left ligamentum flavum at C5-6, producing dorsal spinal canal impingement with nerve root and spinal cord compression. T2-hyperintense cord signal was reported at C5-6. The record does not provide a stenosis grade. This finding correlates highly with the reported progressive myelopathic symptoms.

neurology.localization: Cervical myelopathy at C5-6 due to dorsolateral extradural compression from ossified ligamentum flavum, with bilateral corticospinal tract signs (hyperreflexia all limbs, ankle/toe weakness) and spinothalamic sensory level below C5; posterior columns spared, consistent with central cord involvement; a superimposed radiculopathy cannot be excluded.

red_flags.finding: Ossification of the nuchal ligament at C3-4.
red_flags.rationale: Incidental spinal finding separate from the C5-6 compressive lesion; does not explain symptoms or alter management.

red_flags.finding: Imaging report does not provide a stenosis grade for C5-6.
red_flags.rationale: Without stenosis severity, the urgency and approach of decompression cannot be fully assessed; this influences surgical planning even though the lesion is likely the cause of myelopathy.

neurology.symptom_imaging_mismatch: Dissociated sensory loss (pain/temperature below C5 with preserved posterior columns) is unexpected for a dorsal compressive lesion; a purely dorsal compression would typically involve posterior columns. The pattern suggests central cord involvement, which can occur with compressive myelopathy and cord edema, but the mismatch is noted and may warrant correlation with axial imaging to confirm the extent of intramedullary signal change.
neurology.public_message: Localization is cervical myelopathy at C5-6 due to dorsolateral extradural compression from ossified ligamentum flavum, with bilateral corticospinal and spinothalamic tract signs. Imaging correlates highly (match level high). Red flags: ossified nuchal ligament at C3-4 is coexisting and does not affect management; absence of stenosis grade changes plan because severity is unknown. Note a sensory dissociation mismatch (pain/temperature loss below C5 with preserved posterior columns) that is not typical for dorsal compression but is compatible with central cord syndrome from the lesion; this does not alter the primary localization.

physiatrist_opening.public_message: This patient has progressive cervical myelopathy with cord signal change, which is a concerning finding. However, conservative management may be considered in select cases if the patient is not rapidly deteriorating, as surgery carries risks. We propose a 3-6 month trial of structured physical therapy focusing on gait, balance, and strengthening, along with activity modification and pain management, with close neurologic monitoring. The expected success rate for such conservative treatment in this setting is approximately 20% (based on literature for mild-to-moderate myelopathy, though lower with cord signal change). Failure criteria include any worsening of neurologic deficits, no improvement by 6 months, new bowel/bladder symptoms, or progression on follow-up imaging.

vice_opinions.assessment: This is progressive cervical myelopathy from ossified ligamentum flavum at C5-6 with spinal cord compression and T2 cord signal change. Nonoperative management is unlikely to halt progression and risks permanent deficit. Surgical decompression is indicated.
proposed_options: C5-6 posterior decompression with resection of the ossified ligamentum flavum, without instrumented fusion unless instability is confirmed intraoperatively or on flexion-extension views.
vice_opinions.preferred_option: C5-6 posterior decompression with resection of the ossified ligamentum flavum, without instrumented fusion unless instability is confirmed intraoperatively or on flexion-extension views.
disagreement_points: The physiatrist's proposed 3-6 month conservative trial is not defensible here; progressive myelopathy with cord signal change requires decompression without delay.
vice_opinions.public_message: This patient has progressive myelopathy from an ossified C5-6 ligamentum flavum. Surgical decompression is needed. I recommend C5-6 posterior decompression with OLF resection, fusion only if instability is demonstrated.

director_rulings.final_decision: Proceed with surgical decompression at C5-6. The progressive myelopathy with cord signal change and ossified ligamentum flavum compression is an indication for surgery. The physiatrist's conservative trial is rejected; the 20% success rate is unacceptably low given the risk of permanent cord damage. The absence of a stenosis grade does not change the decision; preoperative flexion-extension radiographs will be obtained to determine the need for fusion. Fusion will be performed only if instability is demonstrated.
director_rulings.surgical_plan: C5-6 posterior decompression with resection of the ossified ligamentum flavum; instrumented fusion only if instability is confirmed on preoperative flexion-extension radiographs or intraoperative assessment.
delegated_tasks: Obtain and review the actual CT/MRI images to confirm the described pathology (resident).
Perform flexion-extension cervical spine radiographs preoperatively.
director_rulings.public_message: The patient has progressive cervical myelopathy due to C5-6 ossified ligamentum flavum with cord signal change. Surgical decompression is indicated to prevent further neurologic deterioration. The physiatrist's proposal for a 3-6 month conservative trial is not appropriate given the low expected success and the risk of irreversible cord injury. I agree with the Deputy Director's recommendation. Preoperative flexion-extension radiographs will be obtained to decide on fusion; if instability is present, fusion will be added. Consent will be obtained with detailed discussion of risks.
